rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Demdeme is the reduplicated form of damma: repeated smearing or coating that surrounds and forcefully covers its object.
rows.anchor: “Demdeme” beyan olunduğuna göre دَمَّ fiilinden mükerrerdir.

rows.speaker: Sıhâh-ı Cevherî
rows.claim: The lexicon glosses demdeme as sticking something to the ground and crushing it by rubbing.
rows.anchor: Sıhâh-ı Cevherî’de der ki: دَمْدَمْتُ الشَّيْءَ أَلْزَقـْتُهُ بِالأَْرْضِ

rows.speaker: Kāmûs
rows.claim: The lexicon explains the verb as grinding a people and destroying them; it also carries wrath and angry growling speech.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs’ta دَمْدَمَ الْقَوْمَ وَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَحَنـَهُمْ فَأَهْلَكَهُمْ

rows.speaker: Müfessirîn
rows.claim: Exegetes understand the repeated coating as bringing sins down upon the people through wrathful punishment, annihilating them completely.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn burada başlıca mükerrer sıvama ve kabri tamamen bastırma mânasından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in fasawwāhā may refer to the punishment, making it cover everyone equally, or to the earth, which was flattened over their dwellings.
rows.anchor: فَسَوَّىٰهَا’daki هَا zamirinin de işaret ettiğimiz vechile “demdeme” masdarına veya

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He finds the pronoun's return to demdeme more apparent, fitting the preceding feminine noun and the image of total punishment.
rows.anchor: “Demdeme”ye rücû‘u daha zâhir ve şu zamire de muvâfıktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not fear the consequence of His punishment or worry that it will bring harm or liability.
rows.anchor: Ve O, onun âkıbetinden korkmaz yani Allah yaptığı ukūbetin âkıbetinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike human rulers who must answer to a superior, God has no power above Him to question or harm Him.
rows.anchor: O’nun mâ-fevkinde O’nu mes’ul edecek, O’na bir zarar verebilecek hiçbir kuvvet ve kudret yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all dominion belongs to God, He acts as He wills and no one can object or intervene; the cited verses affirm this sovereignty.
rows.anchor: Bütün mülk O’nun olduğu için mülkünde لَا يُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's annihilation of the guilty is neither harm to Himself nor injustice to them: He created them and can restore or recompense them, so His judgment is pure justice.
rows.anchor: O helâk ettiği mahlûkātın daha iyisini yaratmaya ve helâklerinden sonra da onlara dilediği sevab

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial waw is resumptive and its pronoun refers to the Lord; the sentence asserts that severe punishment remains fully just despite any apparent objection.
rows.anchor: Bu îzâha göre vâv istînâfiye olarak وَلَا يَخَافُ zamiri “Rabb”e râci‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation treats the wording as a representational metaphor depicting Thamud's abasement, since fear cannot literally be ascribed to God.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ hakkında korku asla mutasavver olamayacağı için bu ifade onların Allah indinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One alternative refers the pronoun to the Messenger: he need not fear the punishment's aftermath because he warned them and fulfilled his mission.
rows.anchor: İkincisi: وَلَا يَخَافُ zamirinin “Resûl”e râci‘olmasıdır

rows.speaker: Süddî, Dahhâk, Mukātil ve Zeccâc
rows.claim: They take the waw as circumstantial and the pronoun as referring to the most wretched man: he did not fear the consequence of his crime.
rows.anchor: Süddî, Dahhâk, Mukātil ve Zeccâc’ın kavillerince vâv hâliye olarak zamir “eşkā”ya râci‘olmaktır

rows.speaker: Müfessirînin bazısı
rows.claim: Some commentators make the Thamud story, with its implied punishment of the Prophet's deniers, the surah's delayed answer to its oath.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînin bazısı, kasemin cevâbı bu Semûd kıssasının medlûlü olmak üzere sûrenin âhirinde mukadder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He instead takes qad aflaha man zakkāhā as the main answer and Thamud as an example proving that purification succeeds while corruption and following rebels end in loss.
rows.anchor: Evvelki vecihte ise قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّىٰهَا وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّىٰهَا kübrâ makāmında asıl cevap

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lesson is to believe and follow God's Messenger and Qur'an, purifying the soul through piety to attain success.
rows.anchor: O hâlde Allah’ın Resûlüne ve nûru olan Kur’ân’a iman ve ittibâ‘

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the Thamud warning suited its first Arab audience because their homeland lay nearby.
rows.anchor: Denilmiş ki bilhassa Semûd kıssasıyla vaaz, ilk muhatab olan Arapların diyarlarına yakın olduğu içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A symbolic reading maps the she-camel to the body, Salih to the spirit, and its watering turn to gnosis, making the story apt to the soul's states.
rows.anchor: nâkatullah bedene, Sâlih rûha, sükyâsı marifete işaret olduğuna göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath may invoke the mighty Creator who made male and female, or, if mā is infinitival, the act of creating them.
rows.anchor: Ve erkeği dişiyi yaratan o büyük kudret sâhibi Hâlık’a yahut “mâ” masdariye olduğuna göre yaradışına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse signals manifestation from unity into multiplicity, including the soul's differentiation into male and female and the scope of the address to both.
rows.anchor: Bunda tecellînin vahdetten kesrete seyrine, ve evvelki sûrede tesviyesi geçen nefsin erkek ve dişiye tenevvü‘üne

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator brings nonbeing into existence and orders multiplicity into unity, showing His oneness and the importance of life's active and receptive pairing.
rows.anchor: yokları var eden ve çoklukları birleştirerek tanzim ve tesviye eyleyen Hâlık’ın birliğine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer warns against scattered effort and urges unified, orderly striving.
rows.anchor: sa‘y ü amelde teşettütten tahzir ile tevhid ve intizâma teşvik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening lām may be an emphatic introductory particle with an implied pronoun, or both lām and sawfa may be understood under an oath; both intensify the promise.
rows.anchor: Bu lâm, وَلَلْءَاخِرَةُ gibi lâm-ı ibtidâ olarak وَلاََنْتَ سَوْفَ يـُعْطِيكَ رَبُّك takdîrinde olması da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says oath-based emphasis is stronger than the introductory lām alone.
rows.anchor: Kasem ile tekid daha kuvvetlidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawfa marks a future event whose realization is certain.
rows.anchor: “Sevfe” istikbalde tahakkuk[^1] ifade eden harf-i tenfistir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming Rabb explicitly where a pronoun could stand renews the address and conveys successive tenderness through acts of lordly care.
rows.anchor: رَبُّكَ isminin zamir yerinde izhârıyla hitâbın iadesi rubûbiyet tecelliyâtının tevâlîsiyle taltif üzerine taltiftir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will give so abundantly that the Prophet reaches complete contentment, with no grief, distress, or waiting left in the enduring afterlife.
rows.anchor: tamamen râzı olacak, rızâya ereceksin bütün dileklerin husûle gelecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This contentment is higher than the station of being content and approved: in divine beauty, all the soul's inclinations unfold toward fulfillment.
rows.anchor: Bu atânın istikbal sîgasıyla ifade edilmesine nazaran kemâl-i uhrevî bir va‘d-i kerîm olduğunda şüphe yoksa da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise also includes worldly gifts: spiritual openings, knowledge, success in proclaiming truth, the Hijra, the conquest of Mecca, and Islam's spread.
rows.anchor: dünyadaki füyûzât-ı nefsiye, ulûm-i evvelîn ve âhirîne vukuf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its greatest importance is the afterlife, where true contentment belongs and recompense is fully given.
rows.anchor: uhreviyede olacağından va‘d u atânın asıl ehemmiyeti de ondadır

rows.speaker: حسن
rows.claim: Hasan interprets the promised gift as intercession.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebî Hâtim’in Hasan’dan tahrîcinde هِيَ الشَّفَاعَة demiştir

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali transmits that the Prophet will intercede for his community until God asks whether he is satisfied; the Ahl al-Bayt identify this verse as intercession.
rows.anchor: Muhammed b. Hanefiyye, Ali keremallahu veche’den bana tahdis eyledi ki

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says one form of the Prophet's satisfaction is that no member of his household enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr’in İbn Abbas’tan tahrîcinde; bu âyette demiştir ki

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas defines the Prophet's satisfaction as his entire community entering Paradise.
rows.anchor: ondan diğer vechile rivayetinde ise onun rızâsı ümmetinin hepsinin cennete girmesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's deep compassion for his community supports these readings of his satisfaction.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalatü vesselâm’ın ümmetine karşı büyük şefkatinin muktezâsı da budur

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet recited Abraham's prayer for followers and Jesus' appeal concerning his people, raised his hands weeping, and prayed for his community; God promised to please him.
rows.anchor: İki elini kaldırdı da اَللّٰهُمَّ أُمَّتِي أُمَّتِي dedi ve ağladı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet can only be pleased with what pleases God; intercession requires divine permission, and God is not pleased with disbelief.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’in rızâsı Allah’ın rızâsındadır. Allah’ın rızâsı olmayan bir hususa Peygamber’in râzı olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intercession report for major sinners encourages no sin; the word 'my community' establishes the value of faith and following, and excludes disbelief.
rows.anchor: de kebâire teşvik için değil, “ümmetî” izâfetiyle iman ve ittibâ‘nisbetinin kıymetini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even unbelievers may benefit from Muhammad's gifts in this world, but without faith that benefit ends here and the afterlife brings loss and severe punishment.
rows.anchor: bu istifade imana iktiran etmedikçe dünyada kalır. Âhiret için hüsran ve azâb-ı azîm olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise does not mean the Prophet should seek indiscriminate forgiveness or demand that Hell be closed; that would promote disbelief and injustice and misuse compassion.
rows.anchor: herkes hakkında bir afv-ı umûmî ilânını istemeli ve cehennemi bütün bütün kapattırmadan râzı olmamalıydı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one may speak before the Merciful without permission and speaking rightly; the cited verse limits intercession accordingly.
rows.anchor: hak ve savab söylemeyenlerin huzûr-ı Rahmân’da tekellüme hakk u salâhiyetleri yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal forgiveness in 39:53 includes disbelief and association, but its following command summons people to repent, submit, and believe; Islam erases past sins.
rows.anchor: bu afv-ı umûmî âyeti, arkasındaki وَأَنِيبُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَسْلِمُوا۟ hitâbıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forgiveness promise is not an invitation to sin; stubborn unbelievers who never repent have no share in it, and neither God nor the Prophet would seek to quench their earned punishment.
rows.anchor: Yoksa zünûb ve me‘âsîye teşvik için değildir. Allah ve Peygamber tanımayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous surah warns that those who deny the good and turn away are eased toward hardship and blazing Fire; this surah's exclusive good for the Prophet warns against them.
rows.anchor: evvelki sûrede وَأَمَّا مَنۢ بَخِلَ وَٱسْتَغْنَىٰ وَكَذَّبَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who follow the Prophet belong to him, as Abraham's statement about his followers illustrates.
rows.anchor: medlûlünce Peygamber’e ittibâ‘eden de ondandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession is a central part of Muhammad's gift, and each community member's share is proportionate to following him.
rows.anchor: bu atâ-i Muhammedîde ümmete şefaat kaziyyesi pek mühim bir asıldır

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: The gift should be read broadly to include worldly favors and the many kinds of afterlife gifts, with the latter far greater.
rows.anchor: demişlerdir ki evlâ olan dünyevî atıyyelere de, türlü envâ‘ıyla uhrevî atıyyelere de umûmudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet can trust that each later stage will be better than the last; the blessings described next demonstrate this pattern.
rows.anchor: olduğu kaziyyesine itmi‘nânı takrir için daha evvelinden meşhud olan ni‘am-i celîle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wājid derives from words for existence, finding, ecstasy, and wealth; God is possessor and agent of existence, knowledge, power, and wealth.
rows.anchor: Bunun asıl meşhur mânası varlık ve buluş ve zenginliktir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later scholars allow calling God mawjūd, though early scholars avoided it because it is a passive form used of created existence; revealed names include Wājid and al-Haqq.
rows.anchor: Menkul olan esmâ-i hüsnâda da “mevcud” ismi vârid olmayıp “Vâcid” ve “Hak” isimleri vârid olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes often take wajada here as knowing: creaturely finding or knowing follows absence or ignorance, which cannot apply to God.
rows.anchor: burada Allah’a nisbet olunan وجد، يجد fiillerini de علم mânasına tefsir etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, the verse means that God knew the Prophet as an orphan and sheltered him.
rows.anchor: Buna göre mâna: “Seni bir yetim bilip yahut

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible but nonstandard reading makes the verb mean bringing into existence, with the Prophet as God's created object.
rows.anchor: Rabbin seni yetim olarak mevcud edip de barındırmadı mı?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers istifā, divine selection: finding a rare valuable thing represents choosing the Prophet from among creatures, a rhetorical emphasis repeated across all three verses.
rows.anchor: burada fikrimizce bunun en muvâfıkı bu fiillerin ıstıfâ mânasına olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatīm means an orphan left alone, and by extension a peerless precious object, as in the unmatched pearl called durr-i yatīm.
rows.anchor: Misli yok gayet kıymetli inciye “dürr-i yetîm” denilmesi de bundandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was born fatherless: Abdullah died in Yathrib while the Prophet was a six-month fetus; his mother died when he was six and his grandfather when he was eight.
rows.anchor: o orada vefat etmişti. O sırada Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem henüz rahm-i mâderde altı aylık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the grandfather's death, Abu Talib took him in as guardian, cared for him attentively, and saw extraordinary qualities in him as a child.
rows.anchor: amcası Hazret-i Ebû Tâlib vasîsi olarak tekeffül edip yanına aldı, güzel baktı

rows.speaker: أبو طالب
rows.claim: In a report to Abbas, Abu Talib describes the Prophet's modesty, fragrant bedding, remembrance of God at meals, honesty, and avoidance of childish play as signs of great grace.
rows.anchor: Ben ondan ne bir yalan ne bir gülmek ne de câhillik görmedim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed couplet says signs of noble character shine in the cradle, witnessing to the grandfather's happiness.
rows.anchor: فِي الْمَهْدِ يعرب عَنْ سَعَادَةِ جَدِّهِ أثَرُ النَّجَابَةِ سَاطِعُ البُرْهَانِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āwā means to gather something to another and lodge or shelter it; God successively sheltered the Prophet after he was orphaned by father, mother, then grandfather, never abandoning him.
rows.anchor: “Îvâ” bir şeyi diğerine zammetmek, ircâ‘eylemek mânasından bir yurda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rhetorical reading hears yatīm also as the peerless pearl: God selected the unmatched Prophet and sheltered his heart in divine care.
rows.anchor: Seni halk içinde nazîrsiz, sadef-i imkânda misilsiz olarak ıstıfâ edip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause coordinates with the positive implication of the first rhetorical question, though it may also attach directly to the verb under lam's negation.
rows.anchor: Evvelki cümlenin hâsılına ma‘tuftur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍāll can mean lost, unsure of the way, or astray, but the Prophet was never intellectually or religiously misguided or morally corrupt.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah hiçbir zaman akl ü dinde sapık mânasına dâll olmamıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the beginning God kept him pure of shirk and desire-driven error; he was a monotheist, never bowed to idols, and was known for virtue and trustworthiness.
rows.anchor: Muvahhid yetişmiş, hiçbir puta secde etmemiş, Allah’tan başka ilâh tanımamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before revelation, despite sound reason, the Prophet lacked revealed knowledge and was perplexed about the true law beyond unaided reason.
rows.anchor: hak din ve şeriatının ne olması lâzım geleceğini ve dünyayı sarmış olan buhran içinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recognized the corruption of pagan Arab religion and the deviation of Judaism and Christianity, yet could not determine the way to truth; the verse refers to this pre-prophetic searching.
rows.anchor: Karşısında bulunan Yahudîlik ve Nasrâniyet, iki dinin çığırından çıkmış olduğunu da sezmişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God selected and guided him by revelation and scripture, teaching what he did not know and showing the straight path.
rows.anchor: Verdiği vahiy, indirdiği kitap ile bilmediklerini bildirerek doğru yolu göstermedi mi?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ā'il can mean poor and needy, or someone with many dependents who themselves are needy; both interpretations are transmitted.
rows.anchor: “Âil” ayle, yani fakr u ihtiyaç sâhibi yoksul, bir de çok iyâl sâhibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation says God selected and enriched the Prophet when he owned little; his trade, Khadija's wealth, Abu Bakr's gift, and later conquests supplied means.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’a pederinden bir nâka ile bir cariyeden başka miras kalmamıştı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later conquests came after the Hijra and thus belong to the future gifts promised in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: Lâkin bu fütûhât, Medine’ye hicretten sonra olduğu için bu sûrenin nüzûlü sırasında değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second interpretation is that God enriched the many needy companions who depended on the Prophet by means of his teaching and guidance.
rows.anchor: birçok iyâlin, muhtac ashâbın var idi. Senin yüzünden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He regards material poverty as the more apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: Lâkin zâhir olan evvelkisidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three blessings show that each later state surpassed the earlier one, assuring the Prophet that this pattern will continue.
rows.anchor: Bunların mâkabline rabtıyla mâna şu olmuş oluyor: Görülüyor ki bunların hepsinde sonu evvelinden hayırlı olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As gratitude for God's present and promised gifts, the Prophet must not oppress or disdain any orphan or waste the orphan's rights.
rows.anchor: Rabbinin bu mevcud ve mev‘ud atâ ve nimetlerinin şükrânesi olmak üzere

rows.speaker: راغب
rows.claim: Raghib defines qahr as either overpowering or humiliating; both senses are prohibited toward the orphan.
rows.anchor: Râgıb’ın Müfredât’ında kahr, galebe ve tezlil ikisidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Prophet experienced orphanhood and God's kindness, he should honor orphans' status and rights rather than treat them as weak or low.
rows.anchor: Çünkü yetimliği tattın ve hakkındaki lütf-ı ilâhîyi gördün

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reports that the verse came after the Prophet raised his voice at a child of Khadija; if even shouting or frowning drew correction, rights violations are worse.
rows.anchor: bu âyet Hazret-i Peygamber Hazret-i Hatice’nin çocuğuna bağırdığı zaman nâzil olmuştur

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet promises a light on Judgment Day for every hair touched when someone strokes an orphan's head.
rows.anchor: Her kim bir yetimin başını

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A report says an orphan's weeping shakes the Throne and God promises to please whoever comforts him; Umar reportedly stroked orphans' heads and gave them gifts.
rows.anchor: Yetim ağladığı zaman onun ağlamasından Arşu’r-Rahmân ihtizaz eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No authentic report specifies the exact manner of stroking an orphan's head.
rows.anchor: Fakat keyfiyyet-i meshi, nasıl sildiği hakkında sahih bir şey vârid olmamıştır

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: The Prophet compares himself and a God-fearing caretaker of an orphan to the index and middle fingers held together.
rows.anchor: Ben ve yetime tekeffül eden şu ikisi gibiyiz, Allah azze ve celle’den korkarsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not scold or drive away a beggar or questioner; meet the need, or refuse gently.
rows.anchor: İsteyeni yahut soranı azarlama, yani azarlayarak kovma da lutfet

rows.speaker: Müfessirînden birtakımları
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the asker to mean a beggar seeking worldly goods, supported by the verse assigning a share to the asker and deprived.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînden birtakımları, sâilden murad dünyaya dair bir şey isteyen dilencidir demişler

rows.speaker: إمام أحمد
rows.claim: Ahmad says the popular report that even a rider has a right to ask has no basis; Abu Dawud transmits it only as a report from Husayn b. Ali, while scholars differ on its chain.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Hüseyin b. Ali radıyallahu anhümâ’dan mevkūfen rivayet edip sükût eylemiş

rows.speaker: ابن مديني
rows.claim: Ibn al-Madini says the report that no one who refuses a truthful asker prospers has no basis.
rows.anchor: “bunun da aslı yoktur” demiş

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits a similar Prophetic report that, were the poor not liars, whoever refuses them would not prosper; the author knows no criticism of this report.
rows.anchor: Ebû Ümame’den merfû‘an ona yakın olan şu hadîsi rivayet eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition applies when the asker is not insistently demanding; if gentle refusal fails, rebuke is permitted because insistence is blameworthy.
rows.anchor: Eğer ilhah eder de redd-i leyyin fâide vermezse o vakit zecirde beis yoktur

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء، الحسن، سفيان
rows.claim: They understand the asker as a seeker of religious knowledge, not only a material beggar; some regard this reading as more apparent.
rows.anchor: Ebü’d-Derdâ, Hasan, Süfyan ve daha birtakımları da burada “sâil”den murad

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report warns that whoever is asked about knowledge and conceals it will be bridled with fire.
rows.anchor: bir ilimden sual olunup da onu ketmeden kimse ateşten bir gem ile gemlenir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sā'il primarily means a beggar but can denote anyone seeking or asking; the preceding mention of material and spiritual needs allows both readings together.
rows.anchor: mutlak “sâil” lafzı dilenci mânasında asıl olmakla beraber dileyen veya dilenen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A true request humbly seeks needed goods or knowledge; a shameless, purposeless, testing, or annoying demand is not the intended question.
rows.anchor: Mal suâli zelîlâne hâcetini istemek mânasına bir dilenmek olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because need and motive are hidden, a question itself gives no right to suspect; initially do not scold or hurt any asker, even if unable to give, and judge only by insistence.
rows.anchor: herhangi bir sual, bir ihtiyaç mânası ifade ettiğinden sâile ilk suâlinde sû’-i zan etmeye hak yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Helping a desperate needy person may become obligatory; knowledge seeking is generally praiseworthy, and a capable answer is obligatory or recommended, while wrongful questioning may be rebuked proportionately.
rows.anchor: Muztar ve muhtâca kudret dâhilinde mümkin olan mu‘âvenet farz mertebesine kadar varabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Material begging is generally blameworthy but permitted for those without another livelihood; able people owe such people help, and until contrary evidence appears any asker must not be mistreated.
rows.anchor: Mal dilenmek umumiyetle mezmumdur. Ancak başka bir kesb çaresi bulamayan muhtaç için bir ruhsattır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tell of the Lord's present and promised blessings through words or deeds that show their benefit to others, to acknowledge and thank God rather than boast.
rows.anchor: Sade lafını ederek ve gösteriş yaparak mağrurlanmak için değil; hakkını takdir, şükrünü îfâ etmek için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final commands follow from God's gifts: show compassion to orphans, give material or spiritual help to seekers, and make the afterlife's superiority known, thereby manifesting God's greatness.
rows.anchor: Rabbinin sana atâ kıldığı gibi yetime şefkat, sâile merhamet, Allah’ın muhtaç kullarına maldan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report through Bezzī traces the practice of saying takbir at the end of Duhā and each remaining surah through Ibn Kathir, Mujahid, Ibn Abbas, and Ubayy to the Prophet; Hakim and others grade it sound.
rows.anchor: Ve’d-Duhâ’ya geldiğimde şöyle dedi: Hatmedinceye kadar her sûrenin hâtimesinde tekbir al

rows.speaker: الشّافعي
rows.claim: Al-Naysaburi reports that al-Shafi'i considered the takbir after Duhā through the Qur'an's end a sunnah; one account connects it with the revelation's return and the Prophet saying Allahu akbar.
rows.anchor: İmâm Şâfiî’den de Ve’d-Duhâ’nın hâtimesinde Kur’ân’ın âhirine kadar tekbîri sünnet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recitation manual recommends takbir after each surah, then after the final surah reciting al-Fatiha and the opening of al-Baqara through muflihun before the completion prayer.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın âhirine kadar her sûrenin hâtimesinde tekbir sünnettir

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi says takbir is optional: reciting it is good and omitting it is harmless; it is sunnah, not Qur'an or an obligation.
rows.anchor: Her kim yaparsa güzeldir, cemîldir, her kim de yapmazsa ona harec yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciters differ on the formula: some say only Allahu akbar, others add the profession of unity, and some include praise.
rows.anchor: bazıları yalnız “Allahu ekber” ile iktifâ eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's reassurance after fear of interrupted revelation stirs gratitude and compassion; its closing takbir can express relief and thanks, provided it is not mistaken for Qur'an or obligatory recitation.
rows.anchor: verilmemek ve farz olarak değil de o zevk ve mânayı duyanların

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reassurance, one must not become idle: hardship comes with ease, and gratitude calls for greater effort, attention to the Giver, and movement toward Him; al-Inshirah follows to continue this lesson.
rows.anchor: her zorluğun yanında kolaylıklar bulunduğunu bilerek tahdîs-i nimet için daha ziyade çalışmak
